faq: Does it account for a blocked horizon?
No — times assume a level, open horizon. A ridge to your east delays your seen sunrise (and the note is printed because valleys live by it). Elevation and obstruction tools refine special cases.
Within about a minute for most inhabited latitudes with the standard solar algorithm — weather and horizon decide what you witness.
Why do sunrise and sunset not shift symmetrically?
The equation of time slides both, so the earliest sunrise and latest sunset fall on different dates (mid-June's bookends straddle the solstice asymmetrically).
Times are reported for the place's clock rules where the tool applies them — and the Sun itself ignores DST entirely, as the base questions on this page note.
Civil, nautical and astronomical twilight each have their own calculator here — sunset is not darkness, and the gap matters.
Inside the circles the Sun can skip rising or setting for weeks — the Polar Day / Night Checker gives the verdict this page cannot print.
Can I get a whole month?
Date by date — or read the shape from the solstice/equinox anchors: the change is fastest at the equinoxes (about 2–3 minutes a day at mid-latitudes).
